note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) species-level description, the original in English; the original uses the old combination Eutermes torresi (now placed in Nasutitermes). The species heading line is broken in the OCR as 'Eutermes tor resi sp. nov.'. Biology records the nest as 'a conical nest, 8—24 inches high', which is not included in the morphology sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) published it as Eutermes torresi, the type locality Thursday Island, Torres Strait. The alate is very large and dark brown, the wings smoky with a yellow costal margin, closely related to E. triodiae but slightly smaller; the soldier is relatively large, with the head and antennae very dark, closely related to E. triodiae but distinguished by the dark colour and the different antennal segmentation.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A very large dark brown species, the wings smoky with a yellow costal margin; closely related to E. triodiae, from which it differs in the slightly smaller size, the darker antennae, and the more numerous, shorter segments that do not form a distinct club. Head and pronotum (Fig. 223) hairy. Compound eyes very large and protruding. Postclypeus length slightly less than half its width. Teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible similar; tooth 2 of the right mandible slightly shorter and wider than tooth 1. Antennae 16-segmented; segments 2—6 variable; segment 3 usually distinctly longer than segments 2 and 4; segments 4 and 6 smallest; segment 5 longer and wider than segments 4 and 6, or segments 2 and 3 about equal in length; segment 7 about as long as segment 5 but narrower, shorter than segments 8—14; segment 15 slightly longer than segment 14; segment 16 about as long as segment 14, narrower than segments 14 and 15. Fontanelle small but usually distinct, forked anteriorly. Media giving off several branches in the apical half. Cubitus usually with 9 branches. Measurements: length with wings 18.50—20.00; length without wings 10.00—12.00; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.83—1.90; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.06—1.21; head width 1.72—1.79; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.60—0.66; ocellus length 0.22—0.24; pronotum length 0.88—0.91; pronotum width 1.61—1.72; forewing length 15.50—17.50; forewing width 4.00—5.00.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A relatively large species, the head and antennae very dark brown, the abdominal tergites strongly pigmented. Closest to E. triodiae, from which it is distinguished by the dark colour and the clearly different antennal segmentation. Head, thorax and abdomen with fairly numerous coarse hairs. Head in dorsal view (Fig. 224) nearly spherical behind the antennae; nasus moderately narrow, slightly less than two fifths of the total head length, the apex dark rusty; head in side view (Fig. 225) concave, slightly convex in the middle. Antennae 14-segmented; segments 1 and 2 red-brown, the remaining segments as dark as the head; segment 2 shortest; segment 3 slightly longer and narrower than segment 2, about as long as segment 5; segment 4 distinctly longer than segments 3 and 5; segment 6 slightly shorter than segment 7; segments 7—9 about equal in length; segments 10—13 shorter than segments 7—9; segment 14 shorter than segment 13. Mandibles with points. Measurements: total length 3.75—4.35; head length (to apex of nasus) 1.76—2.00; head width 1.00—1.32; pronotum width 0.58—0.62.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Upper surface of the head mainly dark brown, paler at the sides; coronal and frontal sutures distinct. Postclypeus pale yellow-brown with a pale brown tinge. Pronotum, mesonotum, metanotum and abdominal tergites brown, slightly paler than the head. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 2 shortest; segment 3 usually distinctly longer than segments 2 and 4. Postclypeus length about half its width. Measurements: total length 5.00; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.94; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.02; head width 1.54; pronotum width 0.91.
